| [CASE-206](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md) v3 | A single flat-foldable degree-4 vertex under a footprint budget: its two folding modes meet only at the flat state, so passing between folded states needs the full flat footprint of 1.866, more than twice what either folded state at 150° takes | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". The minimal toy: one rigid flat-foldable vertex with sector angles 60°, 90°, 120° and 90°, whose configuration space is two folding modes meeting only at the flat state, and a declared resource, the plan area of the smallest convex tray that holds it. Folded states cost 0.75 and 0.875; every switch between them passes the flat state, which costs 1 + √3/2 ≈ 1.866, so the bottleneck budget is 1.866 and the reconfiguration slack 0.991. At a budget of 1.5 the sublevel set cuts each branch near flat and both states are held but neither reaches the other. | [CASE-207](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-207.md) v2 | The square twist: a crease pattern with no rigid folding motion folds once facet bending is paid for, so which configurations are connected depends on the energy available | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Silverberg et al. 2015 ([NOTE-1554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1554.md)): the square twist's crease pattern is isostatic, and rigidly it has only two isolated states, unfolded and folded, yet it folds by bending its facets, a hidden degree of freedom with its own energy scale. The authors' thesis is that the number of degrees of freedom changes with the energy scale probed; their kinematic skeleton, with bending capped at 10°, has a critical plane angle near 23° separating a connected configuration space from a disconnected one. Read as a resource model, the configuration space is indexed by the budget rather than fixed, and widening the admissible moves is itself priced, which joins the vertex under a budget ([CASE-206](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md)) to the curved vertex whose moves no budget widens ([CASE-204](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-204.md)). A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-208](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-208.md) | A prestressed Kresling stack: reordering the cells' energy barriers from outside opens the 8 of 56 transitions between stable states that the barrier order blocked, while the 16 that pass through other stable states are not made direct | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Zang, Zhao, Misseroni and Paulino ([NOTE-1569](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1569.md)): a stack of three bistable Kresling cells has 8 stable states and 56 ordered transitions; 32 are feasible, 16 cannot be made without passing through other stable states, and 8 are blocked by the order of the cells' energy barriers. Springs and handles, applied from outside, prestress the cells and reorder the barriers in place, which makes the 8 blocked transitions feasible; the 16 are not opened. Read as a resource model, the barriers bound the transitions, and the blocked ones are opened by changing the architecture, not by a larger load: the physical counterpart of [CASE-198](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-198.md). Jules et al. ([NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md)) show the same dependence on the order of thresholds in a Kresling memory. A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
